bull_bear.body: The reaffirmation of credit ratings by CARE Ratings Limited is a positive indicator of the company's financial health and stability, and may have a positive impact on the company's stock price and investor confidence.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Adequate captive limestone reserves to meet long-term production requirements, cited by management as the mitigant for input-cost risk
- Captive and green power stack lowering energy cost: 35 MW (17.5x2) captive thermal power plant, 11 MW Waste Heat Recovery plant running at optimum capacity, 13 wind turbines of 13.65 MW and 0.50 MW solar at Aligarh
- Secured sufficient long-term sourcing for its Thermal Coal requirement for the captive power plant
- Brand equity and a balanced mix of retail and institutional sales, with a continually expanding dealer and retailer network
- SAP ERP running core business processes across finance, procurement, sales and supply chain management
- Legacy of the B.K. Birla Group, with senior management associated with the group since 1995
- Recognised mining and environmental performance: Five-Star Rating for the Morak Limestone Mine and multiple 39th Mines Safety Week 2025-26 awards
- Employee attrition maintained at levels significantly below industry benchmarks, on management's own statement
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Key input risk — availability and price of raw materials, fuel and power — Availability and procurement of key raw materials, fuel and other critical inputs at competitive prices are essential for operational efficiency and cost competitiveness; volatility in the prices of fuel, power and raw materials may adversely affect profitability. Mitigated by adequate captive limestone reserves for long-term production requirements, long-standing supplier relationships, and continued investment in process improvements, technological upgradation and fuel efficiency.
- Competition risk — industry capacity expansion pressuring pricing and realisations — The Indian cement industry continues to witness capacity expansion and heightened competition, which may exert pressure on pricing and market realizations. The Company responds with product quality, brand equity, a balanced mix of retail and institutional sales and an expanding dealer and retailer network.
- Economic volatility risk — macroeconomic and geopolitical swings hitting cement demand — Fluctuations in economic growth, inflation, interest rates, currency movements and geopolitical developments may influence industrial activity and impact demand for cement; management monitors the environment and relies on structural drivers such as infrastructure development, urbanisation and housing demand.
- Regulatory and compliance risk — The regulatory landscape continues to evolve with increasing emphasis on environmental, safety, corporate governance and other statutory compliances; any non-compliance could result in financial penalties, legal liabilities and reputational damage. Mitigated by a compliance management framework, internal controls, periodic compliance reviews, internal audits and training.
- Environmental regulation on curbing greenhouse gas emissions — BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications: consumption of limestone and fossil fuels in the manufacturing process leads to release of carbon emissions. Approach is shifting to renewables and/or low-carbon solutions where possible, plus process optimisation and digitisation.
- Climate change / sustainable development — rising fuel, pet coke and coal cost — BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications, rationalised as increasing the cost of fuel, pet coke and coal. Mitigation cited: installation of the Waste Heat Recovery plant, use of biomass, use of wind energy and exploring other green energy options.
- Occupational health and safety — BRSR material issue flagged as both Risk and Opportunity: failure to protect workers from occupational hazards can result in legal action, fines and compensation claims, significant financial liabilities and reputational damage, and can impair attraction and retention of skilled workforce; conversely prioritising well-being strengthens the employer brand. Mitigated through competency development, training, audits, inspections, surveys, We Care initiatives, Critical Control Management and cross-functional process-safety teams.
- Human capital risk — Challenges in attracting, developing and retaining skilled talent may affect operational efficiency and business growth; mitigated by a blend of experienced professionals and young talent, structured recruitment, succession planning, leadership development and continuous training, with attrition stated to be maintained significantly below industry benchmarks.
- Information technology and cyber security risk — Increasing digitalization has heightened exposure to unauthorized access, data breaches, ransomware, phishing, malware, system disruptions and information loss, which could adversely affect business continuity; the Company relies on SAP ERP for core processes and continuously upgrades IT infrastructure, access management, backup, disaster recovery and vulnerability assessments.
- Domestic and geographic concentration — Structural concentration disclosed in BRSR rather than labelled as a risk: cement and clinker account for 96.40% of turnover, operations are national only across six states with no international locations, and exports contribute nil to total turnover.

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells cement and clinker, which account for 96.40% of turnover, and also operates an MDF Division. It serves institutional and commercial customers, dealers, individual house builders and government bodies undertaking infrastructure projects, entirely within India with nil exports. Manufacturing is anchored at Morak (Dist. Kota, Rajasthan), with further units at Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh) and Nabarangpur, supported by captive limestone mines at Morak and Gagrana.
business.title: What they do

business.body:
- Suryadeep RJ1 Projects Private Limited — associate: BRSR item 23 reports NIL holding/subsidiary/associate/joint venture companies; the Company holds more than 20% in Suryadeep RJ1 Projects Private Limited but does not exercise significant influence or control, so it is not construed as an Associate Company. The Company executed a Power Purchase Agreement and acquired the requisite captive equity stake for procurement of solar power under the Captive Open Access framework; Suryadeep has developed a group-captive solar plant at Barmer District, Rajasthan on a Build-Own-Operate basis.
- Vidula Consultancy Services Limited — related party: Enterprise in which Key Management Personnel is able to exercise significant influence; transactions during the year included rent income, rent paid, advance against rent, security deposit given and sale of assets.
- Aranyani Resources Private Limited — related party: Enterprise in which Key Management Personnel is able to exercise significant influence; transactions during the year included raw material purchases, transportation services and advances given for raw material supply (including a refund of advance).
- Mignonette Creations Private Limited — related party: Enterprise in which Key Management Personnel is able to exercise significant influence; purchases for CSR activities and others.
- Anshuman And Vidula Jalan Foundation — related party: Enterprise in which Key Management Personnel is able to exercise significant influence; recipient of donation during the year.
- Rambara Trading Private Limited — related party: Listed as an enterprise in which Key Management Personnel is able to exercise significant influence, with transactions entered during the year.
- AVA Trading and Consulting Private Limited — related party: Listed as an enterprise in which Key Management Personnel is able to exercise significant influence, with transactions entered during the year.
- Pilani Investment and Industries Corporation Limited — related party: Listed company on whose board the Chairman Shri Anshuman Vikram Jalan holds an outside directorship as Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director.
- Dhampur Sugar Mills Limited — related party: Listed company where director Shri Gaurav Goel is Managing Director and Promoter Director; disclosed as his outside directorship (Executive Director).

outlook.body: Outlook: Stable; Strategy: Focus on infrastructure development and construction growth
outlook.title: Guidance / outlook

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the portfolio of premium products while improving operational efficiencies and optimising costs, through sustainable growth initiatives, technological advancements and customer-centric solutions
- Sustainable fuel strategy: further increase use of alternate fuels including biomass and biomass briquettes made from soybean and mustard husk and processed municipal waste, reducing dependence on conventional fossil fuels
- Renewable energy strategy: executed a Power Purchase Agreement and acquired the requisite captive equity stake in Suryadeep RJ-1 Projects Private Limited to procure solar power under the Captive Open Access framework
- Green mobility: replace conventional diesel with biodiesel across plant and mining vehicles and expand battery-operated electric vehicles for in-plant material handling and movement of fly ash and limestone
- Logistics cost optimisation through transportation-mix optimisation, scientific route planning, increased sourcing from primary and nearby locations, renegotiation of commercial arrangements and GPS-enabled tracking and digital monitoring
- Defend pricing in a competitive market through superior product quality, brand equity and a balanced mix of retail and institutional sales, expanding the dealer and retailer network and deepening market penetration
- Maintain adequate captive limestone reserves and long-standing supplier relationships, and invest in process improvements and technological upgradation to optimise raw material consumption and fuel efficiency
- Strengthen the MDF Division's operational and financial performance on the back of improved operating efficiencies
- The Board recommends dividend in accordance with the Company's Dividend Distribution Policy formulated under Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations and published on its website, taking into consideration the Company's financial performance, cash flows, future capital requirements and other relevant financial and non-financial factors; for the year under review it recommended a final dividend subject to shareholder approval at the 50th AGM. The Directors have not proposed to transfer any amount to the General Reserve. On the balance sheet, the Company made repayment/pre-payment of term loans to various banks during the year while continuing to avail long-term and short-term credit facilities from bankers as required, and the AGM notice seeks a Special Resolution under Section 180(1)(c) to increase borrowing limits from the existing `2,000 Crores to `3,000 Crores to fund the purposes of the Company's business. Reinvestment intent is directed at capacity and captive/renewable power, with grinding capacity added at Aligarh, a captive-open-access solar arrangement, and a limestone mining lease bid in Rajasthan.
- ISO standards adopted across the entity: ISO 45001:2018 for Occupational Health & Safety, ISO 9001:2015 for Quality Management Systems and ISO 14001:2015 for Environment Management Systems (all Bureau of Indian Standards), and ISO 50001:2018 for Energy Management Systems (S.G.S, Kolkata)
- Stated intent to contribute to climate change / sustainable development by reducing carbon footprint and using renewable/green energy — via the installed Waste Heat Recovery plant, use of biomass, use of wind energy and exploring other green energy options
- Waste Heat Recovery power plant of 11 MW running at its optimum capacity, lowering power costs and the impact of future fuel and power cost rises
- Aggregate wind turbine capacity of 13.65 MW at Jaisalmer, cited as reducing CO2 emissions
- Group-captive solar: PPA executed and captive equity stake acquired in Suryadeep RJ-1 Projects Private Limited, whose 15.17 MW (AC) / 22 MW (DC) Barmer solar plant is expected to commence supply under STOA by June 2026
- Additional solar capacity of 1.80 MW under installation at the Aligarh Unit, to be completed by June 2026, taking installed solar there to 2.30 MW alongside the existing fully operational 0.50 MW
- Increased use of alternate fuels — biomass and biomass briquettes from soybean and mustard husk plus processed municipal waste — reducing dependence on conventional fossil fuels
- Replacement of more than 50% of conventional diesel with biodiesel across vehicles at cement plants and mining locations
- Expanded deployment of battery-operated electric vehicles for in-plant material handling and for movement of fly ash and limestone
- More than 50,000 saplings planted to create a green belt across manufacturing facilities, mining areas and surrounding communities
- Pollution control: water-mist dust suppression at all raw material transfer points, water sprinkling from harvested water in dust emission areas, and an effluent treatment plant ensuring zero discharge
- Occupational health programme including OPD consultations, silicosis screening camps, periodical health check-ups for staff, workers and contract labour, and community health camps at SohanKheda, Badodiya Kalan, Morak Village and Mangalam Mines
- Adoption of the District Hospital at Ramganj Mandi, contributing to its infrastructure, maintenance and overall development
- EHS Policy founded on full compliance with applicable statutory and regulatory requirements, with a safety culture extended to contract workers, raw material suppliers, transporters and other business partners
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: During FY 2025-26 the Company commissioned an additional cement grinding capacity of 1.20 MTPA at its Aligarh Unit in Uttar Pradesh, taking that unit's total grinding capacity to 1.95 MTPA and the Company's total grey cement manufacturing capacity to 5.60 MTPA; management states the enhanced capacity will let it serve key markets more efficiently, improve market penetration and optimise logistics. On the raw-material side, the Company participated in the MSTC forward e-auction held on 21st April, 2026 under the NIT issued by the Directorate of Mines and Geology, Government of Rajasthan, Udaipur, for a Mining Lease over a Limestone Block at Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, and was declared the "Preferred Bidder" for that lease. On the power side, the Company owns 13 wind turbines aggregating 13.65 MW, a 35 MW (17.5x2) captive thermal power plant for which it has secured sufficient long-term thermal coal sourcing, and an 11 MW Waste Heat Recovery plant running at its optimum capacity. Solar panels of 0.50 MW at the Aligarh Unit are fully operational and a further 1.80 MW is under installation at Aligarh, to be completed by June 2026, taking installed solar capacity at that unit to 2.30 MW. Separately, under its renewable energy strategy the Company executed a Power Purchase Agreement and acquired the requisite captive equity stake in Suryadeep RJ-1 Projects Private Limited, which has developed a 15.17 MW (AC) / 22 MW (DC) solar plant at Barmer District, Rajasthan on a Build-Own-Operate basis under the Group Captive Generation mechanism; that project is under commissioning and is expected to commence supply under the Short Term Open Access mechanism by June 2026, subject to successful stabilisation and necessary approvals.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Cement demand in India is expected to grow by approximately 7%-8% during FY 2026-27, supported by continued momentum in housing, increased infrastructure investment and accelerated execution of Government-led projects
- FY 2025-26 industry growth was driven by sustained demand from rural housing, industrial and commercial (I&C) and infrastructure segments
- Infrastructure remains a key growth driver, with increased capital expenditure across Railways, Road Transport & Highways and Rural Development, and Government infrastructure spending for FY 2026-27 expected to increase further
- Long-term demand underpinned by PMAY, Smart Cities Mission and AMRUT, rapid urbanisation, and continued investment in rural roads, healthcare, sanitation and educational infrastructure supporting rural and semi-urban demand
- Industry added approximately 65 MnTPA during the year to around 730 MnTPA, with nearly 75 MnTPA likely to be commissioned in FY 2026-27 and around 250 MnTPA between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31 to reach roughly 975 MnTPA — capacity expansion and heightened competition that management flags may pressure pricing and realisations
- RBI has projected real GDP growth of around 6.6% for FY 2026-27, with the outlook subject to global developments, commodity price volatility and inflation
- MDF Division outlook for FY 2026-27 remains positive; raw material costs have increased sharply, particularly due to the middle east crisis, which is expected to come down in the near future
- Energy-cost lever from renewable and waste-heat power: the group-captive solar supply is expected to support increased renewable energy usage and lower energy costs

This reaffirmation is expected to have a positive impact on the company's ability to access credit and funding for its future growth plans.

currentContext.expansion: During FY 2025-26 the Company commissioned an additional cement grinding capacity of 1.20 MTPA at its Aligarh Unit in Uttar Pradesh, taking that unit's total grinding capacity to 1.95 MTPA and the Company's total grey cement manufacturing capacity to 5.60 MTPA; management states the enhanced capacity will let it serve key markets more efficiently, improve market penetration and optimise logistics. On the raw-material side, the Company participated in the MSTC forward e-auction held on 21st April, 2026 under the NIT issued by the Directorate of Mines and Geology, Government of Rajasthan, Udaipur, for a Mining Lease over a Limestone Block at Jaisalmer, Rajasthan, and was declared the "Preferred Bidder" for that lease. On the power side, the Company owns 13 wind turbines aggregating 13.65 MW, a 35 MW (17.5x2) captive thermal power plant for which it has secured sufficient long-term thermal coal sourcing, and an 11 MW Waste Heat Recovery plant running at its optimum capacity. Solar panels of 0.50 MW at the Aligarh Unit are fully operational and a further 1.80 MW is under installation at Aligarh, to be completed by June 2026, taking installed solar capacity at that unit to 2.30 MW. Separately, under its renewable energy strategy the Company executed a Power Purchase Agreement and acquired the requisite captive equity stake in Suryadeep RJ-1 Projects Private Limited, which has developed a 15.17 MW (AC) / 22 MW (DC) solar plant at Barmer District, Rajasthan on a Build-Own-Operate basis under the Group Captive Generation mechanism; that project is under commissioning and is expected to commence supply under the Short Term Open Access mechanism by June 2026, subject to successful stabilisation and necessary approvals.

risks.risk: Key input risk — availability and price of raw materials, fuel and power
risks.note: Availability and procurement of key raw materials, fuel and other critical inputs at competitive prices are essential for operational efficiency and cost competitiveness; volatility in the prices of fuel, power and raw materials may adversely affect profitability. Mitigated by adequate captive limestone reserves for long-term production requirements, long-standing supplier relationships, and continued investment in process improvements, technological upgradation and fuel efficiency.

risks.risk: Competition risk — industry capacity expansion pressuring pricing and realisations
risks.note: The Indian cement industry continues to witness capacity expansion and heightened competition, which may exert pressure on pricing and market realizations. The Company responds with product quality, brand equity, a balanced mix of retail and institutional sales and an expanding dealer and retailer network.

risks.risk: Economic volatility risk — macroeconomic and geopolitical swings hitting cement demand
risks.note: Fluctuations in economic growth, inflation, interest rates, currency movements and geopolitical developments may influence industrial activity and impact demand for cement; management monitors the environment and relies on structural drivers such as infrastructure development, urbanisation and housing demand.

The regulatory landscape continues to evolve with increasing emphasis on environmental, safety, corporate governance and other statutory compliances; any non-compliance could result in financial penalties, legal liabilities and reputational damage. Mitigated by a compliance management framework, internal controls, periodic compliance reviews, internal audits and training.

risks.risk: Environmental regulation on curbing greenhouse gas emissions
risks.note: BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications: consumption of limestone and fossil fuels in the manufacturing process leads to release of carbon emissions. Approach is shifting to renewables and/or low-carbon solutions where possible, plus process optimisation and digitisation.

risks.risk: Climate change / sustainable development — rising fuel, pet coke and coal cost
risks.note: BRSR material issue flagged as a Risk with negative financial implications, rationalised as increasing the cost of fuel, pet coke and coal. Mitigation cited: installation of the Waste Heat Recovery plant, use of biomass, use of wind energy and exploring other green energy options.

BRSR material issue flagged as both Risk and Opportunity: failure to protect workers from occupational hazards can result in legal action, fines and compensation claims, significant financial liabilities and reputational damage, and can impair attraction and retention of skilled workforce; conversely prioritising well-being strengthens the employer brand. Mitigated through competency development, training, audits, inspections, surveys, We Care initiatives, Critical Control Management and cross-functional process-safety teams.

Challenges in attracting, developing and retaining skilled talent may affect operational efficiency and business growth; mitigated by a blend of experienced professionals and young talent, structured recruitment, succession planning, leadership development and continuous training, with attrition stated to be maintained significantly below industry benchmarks.

risks.risk: Information technology and cyber security risk
risks.note: Increasing digitalization has heightened exposure to unauthorized access, data breaches, ransomware, phishing, malware, system disruptions and information loss, which could adversely affect business continuity; the Company relies on SAP ERP for core processes and continuously upgrades IT infrastructure, access management, backup, disaster recovery and vulnerability assessments.

Structural concentration disclosed in BRSR rather than labelled as a risk: cement and clinker account for 96.40% of turnover, operations are national only across six states with no international locations, and exports contribute nil to total turnover.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Mangalam Cement Limited is a Rajasthan-headquartered grey cement manufacturer of the B.K. Birla lineage, selling cement and clinker across six Indian states from an integrated Morak plant supported by captive limestone, captive thermal, waste-heat, wind and solar power.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Company manufactures and sells cement and clinker, which account for 96.40% of turnover, and also operates an MDF Division. It serves institutional and commercial customers, dealers, individual house builders and government bodies undertaking infrastructure projects, entirely within India with nil exports. Manufacturing is anchored at Morak (Dist. Kota, Rajasthan), with further units at Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh) and Nabarangpur, supported by captive limestone mines at Morak and Gagrana.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Cement demand in India is expected to grow by approximately 7%-8% during FY 2026-27, supported by continued momentum in housing, increased infrastructure investment and accelerated execution of Government-led projects
- FY 2025-26 industry growth was driven by sustained demand from rural housing, industrial and commercial (I&C) and infrastructure segments
- Infrastructure remains a key growth driver, with increased capital expenditure across Railways, Road Transport & Highways and Rural Development, and Government infrastructure spending for FY 2026-27 expected to increase further
- Long-term demand underpinned by PMAY, Smart Cities Mission and AMRUT, rapid urbanisation, and continued investment in rural roads, healthcare, sanitation and educational infrastructure supporting rural and semi-urban demand
- Industry added approximately 65 MnTPA during the year to around 730 MnTPA, with nearly 75 MnTPA likely to be commissioned in FY 2026-27 and around 250 MnTPA between FY 2026-27 and FY 2030-31 to reach roughly 975 MnTPA — capacity expansion and heightened competition that management flags may pressure pricing and realisations
- RBI has projected real GDP growth of around 6.6% for FY 2026-27, with the outlook subject to global developments, commodity price volatility and inflation
- MDF Division outlook for FY 2026-27 remains positive; raw material costs have increased sharply, particularly due to the middle east crisis, which is expected to come down in the near future
- Energy-cost lever from renewable and waste-heat power: the group-captive solar supply is expected to support increased renewable energy usage and lower energy costs

themes.title: Cement demand & pricing recovery
themes.need: Q1FY27 turned cement from a pricing story into a volume-share-plus-fuel-cost story. ULTRACEMCO grew domestic grey volume +13.1% YoY against an estimated ~7-8% industry, delivered its first Rs 5,000cr+ April-June EBITDA (Rs 5,146cr) with EBITDA/ton held above Rs 1,200, and crossed 200.1 MT domestic capacity a year early - but guided Q2FY27 cost UP ~Rs 130-140/ton and pinned the Rs 1,400/ton consolidated target to Q4FY28. The fuel shock, not price, is the swing factor: JKCEMENT's EBITDA/ton fell to Rs 982 from Rs 1,229 YoY despite +19% grey volume, DALBHARAT flagged pet coke 'surged to nearly $160/t' versus a pre-war $110-115, and NUVOCO defended INR 1,079/ton EBITDA only by cutting petcoke from 37% to 27% of fuel mix in a single quarter. Consolidation is visibly compounding (INDIACEM EBITDA/ton Rs 386->400->509->603 across four quarters; DALBHARAT closed Jaypee at Rs 2,850cr EV with Chunar operational and Rewa on trial within 50 days) even as DALBHARAT slipped its 75mt milestone from FY27 to FY28. SHREECEM/RAMCOCEM/JKLAKSHMI/JSWCEMENT/STARCEMENT/BIRLACORPN ride the same volume + consolidation axis.
themes.driver: Q2FY27 is the guided cost trough - ULTRACEMCO ~Rs 130-140/ton, JKCEMENT ~Rs 150/ton and BIRLACORPN Rs 70-80/ton of incremental cost; then fuel-mix agility (NUVOCO's petcoke swing) and whether DALBHARAT's ~Rs 150/t of procurement savings is really 'permanent, not timing'.
